name: NJM8801 (New JRC / Nisshinbo high-quality audio bipolar dual, 'mass-production MUSES')
tagline: New JRC's bipolar audio dual that applies MUSES know-how to a mass-production process. A Japanese reviewer ranked it above the NJM4580 and below the MUSES8820.
technology: Bipolar-input dual audio op-amp. New JRC says it 'strikes a balance between MUSES technology and mass-production technique', using its own process tuning and assembly technique to raise sound quality without much added cost. Packages are SOP8 (JEDEC 150 mil, 'E') and a small SSOP8 with a copper lead frame ('VA3'). No DIP version is listed.
manufacturers: New Japan Radio Co., Ltd. (New JRC / NJR)

lineage.notes: New JRC placed it among its models that apply MUSES sound-quality techniques to higher-volume processes (stereo.jp 'JRC訪問記'; njr.co.jp product page). The exact release date was not found.

New JRC and Ricoh Electronic Devices merged into Nisshinbo Micro Devices on 1 Jan 2022 (merger date not re-checked in this run). NJM8801 Series is listed on the current Nisshinbo op-amp product pages. The revision and date of the Nisshinbo-branded datasheet were not seen.

reputation.summary: Niche, Japan-centric reputation. New JRC markets it as MUSES know-how moved to a mass-production process, and Japanese sellers call it 'MUSESの量産型' (mass-production MUSES). A Zigsow user review is titled 'NJM4580以上MUSES8820未満' (above NJM4580, below MUSES8820): voicing close to the MUSES8820 but slightly less clear. It also appears in stereo.jp coverage of New JRC. No Western bench measurements were found.
sonic_descriptors: voicing similar to MUSES8820 (one Zigsow reviewer)
slightly clouded / less clear than MUSES8820 (same reviewer)
typical_uses: Vendor-listed applications: audio preamplifiers, reference amplifiers, active filters, line amplifiers
OEM consumer audio: used in Pioneer equipment, sold as a service replacement part (soundservice.gr)
Hobby op-amp swaps as a step up from NJM4580-class parts. Needs an SOP8-to-DIP8 adapter because no DIP version exists.
caveats: The sound claims come from a single Japanese user review plus vendor marketing, so confidence is low.
Surface-mount only (SOP8 'E', SSOP8 'VA3'). Socket rolling needs an adapter, and an adapter can affect stability.
Stability and output-drive limits were not checked against the datasheet.

datasheets.note: This is a Mouser copy under the old 'ds/2/294' path, which Mouser uses for New JRC files. The search summary shows only the title 'NJM8801' and the product description ('a balance between MUSES technology and mass-production technique', 4.5nV/rtHz, 15MHz, 0.0005%). It does not show a Ver. string. The filename suffix 'DataSheetE6' may point to an English edition, but that is not confirmed and it is not recorded as a revision. For comparison, sibling Mouser copies show 'Ver.6.0 http://www.njr.com/' for NJM8080 and 'Ver.3.1' for NJM8068, so New JRC's English datasheets use Ver.x.y numbering. This copy should carry a similar Ver. footer, but it was not seen.

revision_history.changes: Only version identified (Kyohritsu mirror). No change list is visible. Earlier versions, the English datasheet versions and any later Nisshinbo reissue remain unknown.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit reports were found, but no dedicated counterfeit search was run. It is a low-volume, SMD-only, Japan-market part with little grey-market pull, so fakes seem unlikely but are not ruled out. Buy through Nisshinbo-authorized distributors (DigiKey, Mouser) or established Japanese retailers such as Kyohritsu eleshop.
